clue.text: Untrustworthy, like Janus

definitions.meaning: deceitful, saying one thing and doing another
Janus, the Roman god of doorways, is shown with two heads looking opposite ways

explanation.definitionFit: A deceitful person shows different sides to different people, just as the Roman god Janus literally has a pair of heads.

clue.text: Prosperity rising — time passed quickly

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the pieces read upwards, so from the bottom

parts.note: an era is a period of time
time flew means it passed quickly

explanation.surface: Good fortune grew and the years sped by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses ERA FLEW as a whole in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare is wellbeing, a state of doing well.

clue.text: Left a pun lying around as a warning

annotationWithheld.why: Left a pun lying around as a warning: scan reads 'Left a run lying around as a warning (4-5)' for FIRE ALARM, and no reading of the wordplay builds it
annotationWithheld.clue: Left a pun lying around as a warning

clue.text: White downy stuff on twig

definitions.meaning: the soft fibre round the seeds of a plant, spun into thread
twig is British slang for understand; with the clue's on it is the phrasal verb meaning understand

explanation.walkthrough: The 'on' belongs with the answer: to cotton on is to twig, to catch on.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is the white fluffy plant fibre, and to cotton on means to grasp something.

clue.text: Ran indoors when son made to pull back

indicators.note: made in the sense of made into something else, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone ran inside when their boy was forced to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' signals rearranging RAN INDOORS WHEN; the son's S then closes the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw in one's horns is an idiom, from a snail, for becoming cautious and retreating.

clue.text: Oriental dish returns a kiss, very loudly

indicators.note: returns means the pair of words a kiss is read backwards

parts.note: to lip is an old verb meaning to kiss, touching with the lips
ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: An Eastern meal sends back a kiss with great noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns A LIP into PILA; then FF, the musical fortissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaff is a spiced rice dish from the Middle East and Asia.

clue.text: It's invigorating to make my acquaintance

definitions.meaning: a tonic or drink that revives someone
to pick someone up is to strike up a casual acquaintance with them

explanation.definitionFit: A pick-me-up is a reviving drink, and picking someone up is getting to know them casually.

clue.text: Opposed to profit, in a way

indicators.note: in means the profit word is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Someone objects to making money in some respects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' reads as 'in some respects'; the solver must split it so 'in' is the container signal and 'a way' gives the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Against is a preposition meaning in opposition to.

clue.text: Society man with unusual forenames

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A club member has odd first names.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freemason belongs to a fraternal order, the Society of Freemasons.

clue.text: Poet beginning to turn red

parts.note: John Clare was the English nature poet of Northamptonshire

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here of turn

explanation.surface: A poet starts to blush.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine, and by extension a deep red colour.

clue.text: Bill a clergyman? That's right

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
a curate is a junior Anglican clergyman assisting a parish priest

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to send an invoice to a vicar's assistant and is told that is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct, exact, just as right does.

clue.text: Dandy food

definitions.meaning: an 18th-century fop who affected Continental fashions was called this

explanation.definitionFit: The word named both a foppish young man of Georgian Britain (as in Yankee Doodle) and tube-shaped Italian pasta.

clue.text: Hemmed in by Frenchmen, an antelope shows a lot of bottle

indicators.note: something hemmed in by others is enclosed by them, so the Frenchmen go round the rest

parts.note: MM is the abbreviation for Messieurs, French for gentlemen
an gives the letter A
the gnu or wildebeest is an African antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope surrounded by Frenchmen displays great courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for nerve, which the surface leans on; the definition wants a big wine bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a wine bottle holding twice the standard amount, so a large quantity of bottle.

clue.text: Sort of early electrical device

indicators.note: to sort something is to arrange it, so the letters of early are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some kind of primitive electrical gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of early' reads like a vague description, but 'Sort of' signals rearranging EARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay is an electrically operated switch.

clue.text: He gets one old letter late, at the outside

indicators.note: the late word stands on the outside, so the rest goes within it

parts.note: recent means late, as in of late
I is the Roman numeral one
pi is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A man receives a single antique character late, at most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the outside' reads like 'at the most', but here it signals that the word for late wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipient is one who receives, so he gets.

clue.text: Run out of meatballs and trifles

indicators.note: out of means the run letter is taken away from the meatballs word

parts.note: croquettes are fried balls of minced meat or other food
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cook has no more meatballs or sponge puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifles' looks like the dessert but is a verb: flirts. The surface also suggests a shop running out of stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To coquet is to flirt, toying with someone's affections, as one who trifles does.

clue.text: Informed about short time and pay rise — up by 200%

indicators.note: about means the informed word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: told means informed
hr is the short form of hour

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the pay word reads upwards

parts.note: a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: Told briefly about a pay increase that triples wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reverses the pay word, as this is a down entry; 'about' wraps informed round the short time and the reversed pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Threefold means three times as much, an increase of two hundred percent.

clue.text: Liqueur processed in estate

indicators.note: processed means treated and changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drink made on a country property.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Broken romance with MD — the man in charge

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A doctor's love affair has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: A commander is the officer who leads a unit.

clue.text: Man perhaps in crazy trick

indicators.note: in means the Man piece goes inside the crazy word

parts.note: mad means crazy
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, one example of an isle

explanation.surface: A fellow pulls a mad prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' reads as a fellow but is the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead is to deceive, as a trick does.

clue.text: Fresh hole here

definitions.meaning: on a golf course, the cup a player putts into sits on this putting surface

explanation.definitionFit: Green means new or unripe, and in golf it is the closely mown area around each hole.

clue.text: Joy's one of the family right away

indicators.note: right away means the right letter is sent off

parts.note: a relation is a family member

explanation.surface: A woman named Joy is family, straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as 'at once' but splits: R is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness, a synonym of joy.

clue.text: Produce an anagram of litter

definitions.meaning: to rearrange letters, mixing them up
an untidy confused heap of odds and ends

explanation.definitionFit: To jumble is to mix up, as in making an anagram, and a jumble is a disordered mess.

clue.text: Look for this sign for seafood

definitions.text: Look for this sign for seafood

parts.words: Look for this sign for seafood
parts.note: the zodiac sign whose symbol is a pair of fish, read as if it were a sign pointing to a fish restaurant

explanation.definitionFit: Pisces is the zodiac sign of the Fishes, so it suits a clue about seafood.

clue.text: Poet provides accommodation for English doctor

indicators.note: one who provides accommodation houses a guest, so the English letter goes inside the poet

parts.note: A. E. Housman wrote A Shropshire Lad

explanation.surface: A poet puts up an English medic.
explanation.walkthrough: A houseman is the British term for a junior hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseman is a junior doctor resident in a hospital, roughly an American intern.

clue.text: Will of late gave him work

definitions.text: Will of late gave him work

parts.words: Will of late gave him work
parts.note: a testament left by someone recently dead hands this person the job of carrying it out; Will reads like a man's name

explanation.definitionFit: An executor is the person named in a will to administer the dead person's estate.

clue.text: Work that's better

parts.note: a book is a written work
that is, Latin id est, is abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A piece of writing that improves on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like the comparative of good; it is one who bets, and the bookmaker takes the bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker deals in wagers, so is loosely someone in the betting trade.

clue.text: Unsteady walk displayed in old age: in Dorothy retired

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the pair of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: eld is an archaic word for old age
Dot is a short form of Dorothy

explanation.surface: Someone's shaky gait shows in later life, here in a retired woman named Dorothy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses both pieces as one run; ELDDOT read backwards. Eld is an archaic word solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk with short tottering steps like a small child.

clue.text: Parting, the lady would ring

parts.note: she'd is the contraction of she would
ding is the sound of a bell ringing

explanation.surface: On leaving, a woman says she would phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedding means casting off or separating from, a kind of parting.
